https://www.parl.ca/DocumentViewer/en/13.tldr: The One Canadian Economy Act aims to make it easier for businesses to trade across provinces and helps professionals work anywhere in Canada. It also creates a faster process to approve and build major projects that are determined to be in the national interest.
https://www.parl.ca/DocumentViewer/en/13.summary:
Part 1 of the bill focuses on removing barriers to trade and movement within Canada. It establishes that if a product, service, or professional authorization meets the rules of one province, it will generally be recognized as meeting similar federal rules. This is intended to improve efficiency while still protecting the health, safety, and security of Canadians.

Part 2 introduces an accelerated process for 'national interest projects.' If the federal government decides a project is important to the country's economy or security, it can be added to a list that streamlines the approval process. The government must still consult with Indigenous peoples, provinces, and relevant experts, and it must hold independent annual reviews of these projects to ensure transparency.
key_changes: Goods and services that meet provincial standards will be considered to meet comparable federal standards.
Workers with professional authorizations in one province will have those recognized by federal bodies to allow for easier movement across Canada.
A new category of 'national interest projects' is created to help move important infrastructure projects forward faster.
The government can issue a single document that acts as all necessary federal authorizations for an approved national interest project.
The government must publicly provide details, studies, and assessments regarding these national interest projects before final approvals are given.
A mandatory annual independent review of the progress, budget, and timelines for each national interest project will be conducted and reported to Parliament.
